trapping<W, lo‥hi>

Translation status: English reader-locale proof. Term names and code fences follow the en pack; supporting prose may still be English.

A range as the second argument of trapping: a store inside the range keeps its value, a store outside it traps.

Syntax: trapping<i32, -2‥3>

Category#

arithmetic

Related#

  • lo‥hi>"

Examples#

radix/corpus/operatores/ranged-trapping.fab (canonical · operator-group)#

A range as the second argument of trapping: a store inside the range keeps its value, a store outside it traps.

# =============================================================================
# trapping<W, lo‥hi> — a store outside the range traps
# =============================================================================
#
# What this teaches:
#   • A bare integer type is `trapping` over its whole width; a range narrows
#     the cells it accepts. `trapping<i32, -2‥3>` holds -2 to 2: a cell for a
#     step, an offset or an index that must stay in bounds.
#   • A value in the range is stored as is. One outside it traps at the store
#     (see `ranged-trapping-trap`); nothing is clamped or wrapped.
#   • Arithmetic is exact. `dy + dz` can leave the range and prints exactly;
#     only a store into a ranged cell checks it.
#   • A ranged cell reads as its width: it passes where an `i32` is wanted, and
#     it widens into a cell with a wider range without a check.
#   • `u8` is the same type as `trapping<u8, 0…255>`.
#
# Common mistakes:
#   • Expecting a trap in the middle of an expression — the range is checked
#     where a value is stored into the cell, not where it is computed.
#   • Writing a range on a float width — `trapping<f32, 0‥8>` is refused.
#
# See also: trapping, saturating, wrapping
# =============================================================================

fn offset(trapping<i32, -2‥3> dy) → int {
    return dy
}

fn grow(trapping<u8, 0‥10> small) → trapping<u8, 0‥20> {
    return small
}

main {
    let i32 d ← 2
    let trapping<i32, -2‥3> dy ← d
    let i32 e ← -2
    let trapping<i32, -2‥3> dz ← e
    print dy
    print dz
    # Exact arithmetic: 4 is outside -2‥3 and prints as 4; nothing is stored.
    print dy + dy
    # A ranged cell reads as its width.
    let i32 back ← dy
    print back
    print offset(-2)
    # The inclusive glyph holds its high end.
    let trapping<u8, 1…5> top ← 5
    print top
    # Widening a range needs no check.
    let trapping<u8, 0‥20> larger ← grow(7)
    print larger
    # A ranged cell indexes a list: it can only name a slot inside its range.
    let list<int> xs ← [10, 20, 30, 40]
    let trapping<u8, 0‥4> ix ← 2
    print xs[ix]
    # The whole-width range is the bare type.
    let trapping<u8, 0…255> same ← 200
    let u8 plain ← same
    print plain
}

Expected output:

2
-2
4
2
-2
5
7
30
200
